references.text: The same context regarding the Passover meal, where it is stated that no foreigner shall eat of it, which is further elaborated in verse 45 concerning residents and hired workers.
Shows that a foreigner who wishes to participate in the Passover meal must be circumcised, unlike the resident and the hired worker who do not have this option without circumcision.
Uses the same terminology for 'toshav' (resident) and 'sakir' (hired worker) in connection with holy offerings that the priest is not to share with them.
Mentions 'toshav' and 'sakir' together in the context of the sabbatical year, showing these categories of non-Israelites who lived among the people.
Uses the same terms 'toshav' and 'sakir' to describe an Israelite who sells himself, illustrating the status of these groups.
Exodus 29:33 confirms the principle in Exodus 12:45 that foreigners are excluded from holy sacrificial meals.
